Article Title: Years after telling Meta employees to inflict pain on Apple, Mark Zuckerberg sends 'thanks note' to Apple CEO John Ternus; gets a 'reply'
Article Text:
Apple and Meta are on speaking terms again

Meta's most capable open AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio

Apple's privacy push cost Meta billions and sparked years of barbs

A former Apple executive helped bring Meta and Apple back to the table

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has publicly thanked Apple 's new CEO John Ternus , and Ternus has written back. The exchange happened on X on Thursday, when Meta released the weights for Muse Spark Open. That's Meta's new open-weight AI model, and the two companies spent months tuning it to run locally on Apple's Mac Studio desktops. Zuckerberg shared a picture of Meta's AI agent at work on a Mac. He wrote that the model "runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple."Ternus took over from Tim Cook last month. He replied "Congrats to the team!" and said Mac Studio "keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI." It is a far cry from 2021. That year, Apple's App Tracking Transparency feature hit Facebook's ad business, and Zuckerberg reportedly told employees the company needed to "inflict pain" on Apple.Muse Spark Open is an 816-billion-parameter model built on a mixture-of-experts design. Meta calls it the most capable US-developed open-weight model to date. It is aimed at long coding sessions, multi-step reasoning and video analysis. The model is free to download from platforms like Hugging Face, and its licence allows commercial use with some limits.The setup links two or four Mac Studios running Apple's M5 Ultra chip.Apple's MLX framework splits the model across those machines. Apple has also put out new benchmarks and technical notes on how MLX handles open models of this size. Since everything stays on the desk, Meta does not see the prompts or files developers feed it. "Meta has no control or visibility to any of that," Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said.It does not come cheap. An M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 256GB of memory costs over Rs 9 lakh at US prices, and the model needs at least two. A 512GB version is due later this month.The bad blood goes back years. In 2018, at the height of the Cambridge Analytica scandal, Cook was asked what he would do in Zuckerberg's shoes. "I wouldn't be in this situation," he said. Zuckerberg called the remark "extremely glib."Then iOS 14.5 arrived in 2021. It made apps ask permission before tracking users across other apps and websites, and most iPhone owners chose not to be tracked. Meta later estimated the change would cut its 2022 revenue by $10 billion. As recently as last year, Zuckerberg told podcaster Joe Rogan that Apple "hasn't invented anything great since the iPhone."The two have not struck a public partnership since 2017, when Apple pulled Facebook's built-in integration from iOS.Wang credits Daniel Gross with getting the two sides to work together. Gross is a former Apple executive who joined Meta's AI push last year. "Most of the animosity predates my tenure at the company," Wang said in an interview. He added that he was "excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again."Both sides get something here. Apple gets to show its chips can handle heavy AI work away from Nvidia-powered data centres. Meta gets its model in front of developers who might later pay to scale up. Apple already uses Google's Gemini models in Apple Intelligence, and its relationship with OpenAI has ended up in court.Neither company would say if more is coming. The real test would be Meta's models showing up inside Apple Intelligence. For now, the change is mostly one of tone. Five years after talking about inflicting pain on Apple, Zuckerberg is tagging its CEO by name, and Ternus is replying with exclamation marks.
Article Summary: Meta's most capable open-weight AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio. Zuckerberg shared a picture of Meta's AI agent at work on a Mac. He wrote that the model "runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple"

Article Title: In a solar-simulator test, aluminum cooling fins raised a panel’s output 11.5%; adding folded plastic bags lifted the increase only slightly, to 11.6%
Article Text:
AI Representation: A photovoltaic panel fitted with aluminum cooling fins and folded plastic bags at the rear. Image credits: Chatgpt

Aluminum fins helped release heat from the panel

Investigation of Repurposed Material Utilization for Environmental Protection and Reduction of Overheat Power Losses in PV Panels

Aluminum fins and folded plastic bags increased output power by 11.6%

Lower panel temperatures can improve electrical performance

A real solar simulator in a university clean-energy laboratory. Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Outdoor testing is needed to establish practical benefits

Solar panels can lose some of their electrical performance as they heat up under strong sunlight. Scientists have tried several ways to limit heat on panels without electric cooling, including using affordable materials that would normally be thrown away. One study used a cheap combination of aluminum heat sinks and folded plastic bags mounted on the rear of a solar panel. These results suggest that a non-electric cooling system can improve solar panel performance, at least under laboratory conditions. Discarded plastic bags could thus have another application in managing heat.A 2019 study by Ammar Alkhalidi, Mohamad K. Khawaja and Abdel Ghaffar Al Kelany,, published in the International Journal of Photoenergy , examined whether repurposed plastic materials could help cool photovoltaic panels and reduce heat-related power losses. The researchers tested the panel under halogen-lamp simulator conditions, then added fitted heat-extraction fins before layering in repurposed HDPE and plastic bags.They report that this passive cooling approach lowered panel temperature and raised power output at 1000 W m⁻², with the perforated fin design chosen for its lower weight and better airflow. The perforated aluminum fins were attached to the back of the panel to increase its surface area for heat exchange, and the perforations let air move through them.No fans or pumps were used because the cooling method was passive.The biggest performance increase came from combining aluminum cooling fins with folded plastic bags on the back of the panel. At a simulated irradiance of 1,000 watts per square metre, this configuration produced 11.6% more output power than the unmodified panel and lowered the panel’s temperature by 22.7%. Aluminum fins alone raised output power by 11.5%, so the bags added only a small further gain. The study also tested the fins with ground HDPE, but the highest output came from the folded plastic bags.Heat management matters because photovoltaic modules generally lose electrical performance as their operating temperature rises. The review On the temperature dependence of photovoltaic module electrical performance: A review of efficiency/power correlations by E. Skoplaki and J. A. Palyvos, published in Solar Energy in 2009, examines the relationship between module temperature, electrical efficiency, and power output. In the opinion of the authors, the review is dedicated to one-sun commercial silicon modules and considers how temperature affects the major electrical characteristics, particularly efficiency and maximum power. The review also emphasizes the typical test condition of 25°C and 1000 W/m² and explains the temperature effect using the well-known negative temperature coefficient.The energy production of solar panels requires sunlight, but the heat caused by high irradiance lowers their voltage and peak power. Thus, removal of excessive heat could enable a panel to produce more efficient electric energy using the same amount of sunlight. In the above-mentioned study by Alkhalidi and colleagues, the possibility was tested with a passive cooling system made of aluminum fins and plastic. Since this system did not use any equipment for active cooling, it had the potential to increase the efficiency of panels without requiring additional electricity consumption. But the observed effect was reached only in a laboratory setting, not necessarily reflecting results that could be achieved in outdoor installations due to variations in sunlight, air moisture, and wind.The combination of these materials with aluminum fins represents a simple way of temperature control and reuse of waste material. There are some practical issues that need to be investigated. For example, how does the change of outdoor conditions such as varying light, wind, dust, and humidity influence the cooling process? The researchers should study the system's durability, maintenance, and costs of its installation before determining its feasibility. This experiment showed that a passive cooling system using aluminum fins and folded plastic bags can increase a solar panel’s power under laboratory conditions.
Article Summary: Solar panels can lose some of their electrical performance as they heat up under strong sunlight. Scientists have tried several ways to limit heat on panels without electric cooling. One study used a cheap combination of aluminum heat sinks and folded plastic bags mounted on the rear of a solar panel. The results suggest that a non-electric cooling system can improve solar panel performance.

Article Title: In the early 2000s, California man Elmer Long turned his father’s bottles into a public two-acre ranch; today, more than 200 welded trees display over 1,000 bottles
Article Text:
Elmer's Bottle Tree Ranch in Oro Grande, California. Credits - Wikimedia Commons

From one tree to a forest

AI generated representative image. Credits - Gemini

Keeping the ranch standing

The Mojave Desert appears to be as desolate as it gets when you drive along the former National Trails Highway between Barstow and Victorville. Then there's a bottle forest at the side of the road. On a windy day, the entire area whistles as glass in every colour hangs from welded metal trees. It appears museum-worthy, but anyone can enter.This is Elmer’s Bottle Tree Ranch in Oro Grande, California, built using bottles his father collected and left behind. Long began creating bottle trees around 2000. Today, the free, two-acre site features more than 200 trees displaying over 1,000 bottles. Arts charity SPACES calls the place filled with hundreds of welded trees adorned with bottles and miscellaneous artefacts. The story behind the ranch begins with Long’s desert boyhood and his father’s collecting.A father’s desert hoardIn the 1950s, Elmer camped in the Mojave with his father, aircraft engineer Elmer Long Sr., who loved the desert. The two collected anything that caught their eye, including bottles, and noted where each find was located. The elder Long aged and began to pass out the bottles. His son chose to rescue the remains and transferred them to his house on Route 66 near Oro Grande.The bottles, metal pipes and antiques remained in storage until Long found a way to turn them into a display.Around 2000, Long attached bottles to a wooden post to create his first bottle tree. The following morning, sunlight shining through the glass inspired him to make more. Roadside America reports that travellers stopped to photograph the display that same day. By 2002, Long was creating bottle trees full-time. Long’s first bottle tree used a wooden post, but the ranch eventually grew into a forest of more than 200 trees made from metal pipes with welded branches, according to accounts from Amusing Planet Bottles were just the start. The ranch also features a boat filled with bottles, a tree made from a discarded missile casing, and toppers ranging from an electric guitar and a surfboard to a gumball machine. The collection combines objects recovered from roadsides and landfills with decommissioned weapons and other military hardware documented in the SPACES archive.Long was not the first person to string bottles on trees in this part of the desert. Miles Mahan, a retired funfair worker, started creating Hula Ville in 1955 on a half-acre plot outside Hesperia, featuring bottle trees, painted rhymes and recovered signs. Some Route 66 writers have suggested that Hula Ville may have inspired Long, but the connection remains unconfirmed. Hula Ville was razed in September 1997, but some of it was spared and can be seen, SPACES notes, at the California Route 66 Museum in Victorville.Elmer Long passed away on June 22, 2019, at the age of 72 after a battle with lung cancer. The ranch was reopened in early September of that year, with his son Elliott taking command. The ranch is free to enter when its gates are open, and a wishing well on the grounds accepts donations.Elliott has been upfront about how hard that is. He wrote on the ranch’s website that time, weather, neglect and the cost of keeping a property for free are catching up quicker than he can keep up. He estimated the deferred maintenance at roughly 150 hours of work, Route 66 News said. In an update in May 2026, he noted the gates have remained open largely thanks to a site manager named Brian and praised the additional travellers expecting when Route 66 hits its centenary.Route 66 turns 100 on 11 November 2026, which makes this a fitting moment to visit. The ranch sits at 24266 National Trails Highway in Oro Grande. There are no official hours, but the gates are usually open in daylight, and on days they are shut, you can still see much of it through the fence. Elmer Long never set out to create a monument. He had his father's bottles, some pipe put away and a post to try them on. What resulted was a free roadside attraction that drivers still stop to see.
Article Summary: Elmer’s Bottle Tree Ranch in Oro Grande, California, built using bottles his father collected and left behind. Today, the free, two-acre site features more than 200 trees displaying over 1,000 bottles. The ranch is free to enter when its gates are open and a wishing well on the grounds accepts donations.

Article Title: A Buckinghamshire wildlife garden redesigned around an unheated natural swimming pond that attracts frogs, bats, and dragonflies
Article Text:
Image: Julie Skelton

A wildlife and wellbeing brief, how Rachel Platt connected a Buckinghamshire garden to the countryside

Inside the unheated natural swimming pool, a plant-free swim zone and a planted regeneration zone

Frogs, toads, newts, dragonflies, bats, and birds, all the wildlife that has moved into the garden's ponds

The existing terrace and two ponds were kept for their environmental value (Image: Julie Skelton)

How drainage reshaped the plan and kept old favourites

Edible hedgerow, uncut winter meadow, and autumn colour; planting that completes the wildlife garden

A place where the daily swim could begin at the back door, surrounded by dragonflies and flowering plants, even in winter, was the dream of two owners in south Buckinghamshire, who work in the veterinary sector and wanted a garden connected to the surrounding fields. Garden designer Rachel Platt answered with an unheated natural swimming pool, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an edible hedgerow. The result attracts frogs, bats, dragonflies, and more. Read on to discover how the design works, which plants and features support wildlife, what changed along the way, and how the owners describe their transformed outdoor sanctuary. The garden shows how thoughtful landscaping can combine everyday enjoyment with a thriving habitat, creating a peaceful retreat that evolves with the seasons.According to Homes and Gardens, which featured the project in an article by Rachel Bull, the owners both work in the veterinary sector and dreamed of a garden linked to the rolling fields and hedgerows around them. Their brief asked for a biodiverse landscape that would support wildlife while also providing space to swim, grow food, entertain, and spend more time outdoors. Rachel Platt Garden Design responded with a layout that deliberately changes character as it moves away from the house: stronger geometry near the building gives way to softer curves, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an experimental edible hedgerow toward the fields beyond.Before the redesign, the owners regularly drove elsewhere to swim in rivers and spent relatively little time in their own garden, so the new design was meant to bring that experience home.At the heart of the garden sits an unheated natural swimming pool, created as both a wildlife habitat and a place for the owners to reconnect with nature, Homes and Gardens reports. Designer Rachel Platt developed it in collaboration with Ellicar Natural Pools. The pool is divided into a swim zone, kept clear of plants and wildlife, and a regeneration zone planted with a range of aquatic species that filter the water naturally, a process the article calls hydrobotanical filtration. Around the shoreline, water mint, water forget-me-nots, native flag irises, marsh marigolds, ragged robin, and purple loosestrife add colour, seasonal structure, and fragrance, flowering from March to September and attracting pollinators and moths. Deeper-growing aquatics such as common water plantain and arrowhead offer late summer flowers and seedheads, and give emerging dragonflies stems to climb while they unfurl their wings.The wildlife has arrived in force. Homes and Gardens reports that dragonflies and bats were already drawn to the pool, with planting softening its edges and tying it into the wider ecosystem. The owners told Homes and Gardens that frogs, toads, and newts breed in all the ponds, as do several dragonfly species, and that they have even spotted a water snake. Birds also visit, using a beach area, a feature not found in conventional ponds, to enter the water and bathe safely. The owners described the pond as a total escape through every season, and said the garden has become a haven where they feel miles away from everything. For anyone planning a wildlife garden, the lesson is that a single well-planned water feature can support amphibians, insects, mammals, and birds at the same time.The pool was not always meant to be round. According to Homes and Gardens, the original concept was a formal linear pond positioned to reflect a mature birch tree visible through large French doors off the open-plan kitchen and living space. Existing drainage and a suspected utility service running across the garden forced a rethink, and the design became a circular pool. Sustainability and sentiment guided other decisions too. The existing terrace and two ponds were kept for their environmental value and the wildlife they support, and much of the existing planting was saved or relocated, including the owners' fig tree, lily of the valley, raspberries, and rhubarb. Reusing what already works reduces waste and preserves habitat, while keeping familiar plants gives the new garden a sense of continuity with the owners' past.Beyond the pool, an edible hedge links the garden to the landscape, Homes and Gardens says, combining common hazel, hawthorn, blackberry, black chokeberry, damson, pear, and serviceberry to provide structure, blossom, fruit, and habitat. It leads gradually into the meadow, which the owners deliberately leave uncut over winter so that insects, birds, and small mammals can feed on seeds and find a place to overwinter. Autumn colour was also requested, so ornamental grasses such as Miscanthus 'Beth Chatto' and perennials such as Ceratostigma plumbaginoides and white gaura carry warm tones, while burning bush adds bright red. A kitchen garden, grapevine pergola, firepit, and outdoor shower complete the picture. Summing up the transformation, the owners told Homes and Gardens, "We really have our own little Eden," and called the redesign the best decision they have ever made.
Article Summary: Two owners in Buckinghamshire wanted a garden connected to the surrounding fields. Garden designer Rachel Platt designed an unheated natural swimming pool, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an edible hedgerow. The result attracts frogs, toads, newts, dragonflies, bats, and birds.

Article Title: Princeton University's PhD degree holder says he applied to 2300 jobs in two years, got no response; Father says he never thought in million years...
Article Text:
Jack Weis, a PhD degree holder from Princeton, found no jobs in last two years.

Both parents are physicians; they are shocked

30-year-old Jack Weis has a Dr before his name but no job to sustain himself. A Princeton University PhD holder in chemical engineering, Weis applied to over 2300 jobs since graduating in 2024 but found no luck. His research is tied to a Nobel Prize, but Weis told The Wall Street Journal that he was open to a software engineer role and even food preparation roles. Weis graduated summa cum laude from Rice University and then enrolled at Princeton in 2028 for his doctoral studies. Weis' research into ice formation was cited as an illustration of machine learning's scientific applications in connection with the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics.In January 2026, Weis got a part-time job earning $70 per hour at a startup where he was working as a specialist to train AI. He told Journal that he was working 20 hours some weeks and four hours other weeks, depending on the workflow. But eventually, jobs dried up and then by mid-March, he was notified that his contract was going to be terminated.Weis is now considering studying law and also planning to start something on his own.He wants to design AI drone to remove invasive weeds. "If you believe something has true value, you have to step up and realize that value yourself," he said.Dr Weis' parents are both physicians and they are surprised to see his employment struggles. His mother Holly Carvers went through the son's CV and found that it was well-written and there's nothing that may discourage employers from hiring him. His father, John Weis, said, "I never in a million years thought this kidUnemployment was 4.2% in September, up 0.1 percentage point from August, according to the September jobs report released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics on Oct. 2. Total employment grew by 29,000 — well below economists’ forecast of 84,000. In addition, July’s hiring numbers were revised down by 31,000 to -10,000, while August was revised down by 29,000 to 133,000. Together there were 60,000 fewer jobs added in July and August than originally reported.

Article Title: US entrepreneur Morissa Schwartz used AI assistants to make her working day easier, but her to-do list grew to 156 tasks; she now caps it at 25 and says completing work matters more than planning it
Article Text:
Fortune

Her to-do list hit 156 items

Proof before checkmarks

Every few weeks, another AI assistant promises to take a task off your plate. The promises are tempting: it can draft the email, sort the inbox and plan the week. The question is no longer whether these tools can do the work. It’s whether they are lightening the load or quietly adding to it. Morissa Schwartz, an entrepreneur, author and AI strategist, recently discovered just how easily an attempt to improve productivity can turn into another job. “I believe in AI. But my AI assistant gave me more work than it could finish. I opened my daily to-do list and found 156 items,” she wrote inDespite having AI assistants to manage her workload, she found her daily to-do list flooded with 156 items. Instead of making her work easier, her AI assistant had created a growing list of tasks. The reminders and follow-ups threatened to overwhelm the very system designed to keep her organised.Morissa Schwartz explained how asking AI to help with a project often leads to a plan, which is then followed by a checklist and eventually a series of additional tasks. Though each may appear useful individually, the growing list can turn productivity management into another task.She isn’t against technology. Her complaint is that an assistant can produce work faster than anyone can finish it. Her fix was to cap her daily list at roughly 25 meaningful entries and ask a sharper question about every task: what would ‘done’ look like to the person who asked for it? In her profession as a publisher, that would mean a finished draft. If the request was to pitch it, done means the pitch was sent.She revealed how she retrained her AI assistants. “Here are the changes I’m making. First, I want a daily list that reflects available capacity. For assistant execution, I’m aiming for roughly 25 meaningful entries on a weekday, while preserving real deadlines and necessary daily operations. The number is a working limit for my system, rather than a productivity prescription for everyone.” Its purpose was to force her system to prioritise tasks instead of treating everything as equally urgent. “If everything is due today, the list has stopped helping me decide what to do today.”Flexible work also moves into a backlog with a regular checkpoint. Items waiting on someone else get a waiting status rather than a place at the top. Related steps, such as research, outreach and follow-ups for a single campaign, are grouped under one execution item. The details stay available, but they stop competing for attention. “A genuine deadline deserves space that has not already been occupied by 40 vaguely urgent reminders,” she wrote.Her second rule is to group related tasks under one main item instead of listing each one separately. For instance, research, outreach and follow-ups for a campaign could be managed under a single task, keeping the to-do list shorter and easier to manage without losing important details.Third is, of course, evidence. If the assistant says an email went out, she wants to see it in the sent folder. If something was published, she wants the live link. If a file was delivered, she wants the usable file and a record of the delivery. It’s not that she does not ‘trust’ her agents. Rather, she believes evidence matters. “That proof also helps prevent duplicate work. A system that remembers what actually happened can stop proposing the same action with slightly different punctuation,” she wrote.Fourth, a ‘blocker’ needs to be specific. “‘Unable to complete’ gives me another mystery to manage. ‘The form requires an answer only you can provide’ gives me a decision. ‘This browser session cannot access the account’ identifies an access problem,” she said. She wanted the AI to explain clearly why a task could not be completed, whether it needed her input or had an access issue. This would help her solve the problem quickly without delaying other tasks.Finally, Schwartz measures outcomes. How many pitches went out? Which replies still need an answer? What was accepted? Which deliverables reached the client? What remains unfinished? “I care about those numbers because they describe the work I was trying to accomplish. A magnificent list of possible actions describes the system’s imagination,” she said.Schwartz is not arguing that AI should do less. She still wants an assistant. What she wants is one that rewards finishing, checks its own claims and says plainly what is left. By her measure, a good day has fewer items on the list and a clearer record of what was sent, published or delivered.
Article Summary: Morissa Schwartz, an entrepreneur, author and AI strategist, recently discovered just how easily an attempt to improve productivity can turn into another job. She found her daily to-do list flooded with 156 items. Her fix was to cap her daily list at roughly 25 meaningful entries and ask a sharper question about every task.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

Is Aadhaar mandatory for a digital Life Certificate



Legal validity of Jeevan Pramaan



How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
Article Text:
Japan’s adult nappy production and South Korea’s pet-stroller sales reveal shifting demographics (AI-generated image)

When adult nappies overtook baby nappies

illustration

Pet strollers sell more than baby strollers

Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply.They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.
Article Summary: In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales.

Article Title: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang praises Mark Zuckerberg, he replies: I have never gotten such a nice…
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang

‘ Very Bayesian ’: Rapid decisive conviction

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and company CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision-making. During a recent interview, Meta’s Wang was asked about the qualities of Facebook founder, and he offered glowing praise for Zuckerberg, highlighting his exceptional willingness to make massive, rapid pivots based on core convictions. During the conversation Wang was specifically asked how Zuckerberg differed as a leader from what he initially anticipated. Before Wang could reply, Zuckerberg opened with a lighthearted quip, joking, “I think I can leave now.” Wang quickly followed up with his perspective on their working relationship over the past year.Wang noted that while he does not have an extensive set of comparisons, observing Zuckerberg's management style firsthand revealed unique traits that stand out even within elite tech founder circles:“One of the very cool things about working with Mark over the past year has just been watching the true degree of his boldness,” Wang explained, adding, “Once he internalises certain beliefs, like the speed and magnitude of willing to change prior actions and pivot towards the worldview that is consistent with those beliefs, I think these are pretty unusual traits, generally speaking, even among this base of founders. Very Bayesian.”The analytical praise drew a warm, humorous reaction from Zuckerberg.“Very Bayesian. I've never gotten such a nice compliment,” Zuckerberg responded.A person who follows the Bayesian method relies on statistical inference, using Bayes' theorem to update the probability of a hypothesis as new data or evidence becomes available.Expanding on his observations, Wang admitted that Zuckerberg's appetite for sweeping strategic gambles initially took him by surprise before earning his deep respect.“No, but then I think also just the degree of boldness. It was actually quite puzzling to me at first, the degree to which you were willing to make these massive bets. That is quite a notable trait and something I really admire,” Wang continued.Zuckerberg concluded the exchange with appreciation for the assessment, replying: “I'm so flattered.”
Article Summary: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision- making. Article Title: Microsoft says AI agents inside companies can’t be trusted, wants ‘Guardian Agents’ to watch their moves
Article Text:
Guarding the companies with ‘Guardian Agents’

At a time when there is a growing wave of publicly disclosed safety incidents highlighting the sheer power and potential hazards of modern artificial intelligence (AI) and AI agents, cybersecurity experts are sounding the alarm on an overlooked vulnerability: the autonomous software agents operating inside corporate networks. While the broader tech industry has remained fixated on external cybercriminals weaponizing models, companies have quietly deployed thousands of internal agents to handle everyday business processes. Microsoft says that since these agents were implemented internally, organisations have largely treated them with implicit trust, there is a need for ‘Guardian Agents’ to make matters more secure.When optimised purely to attain targets, AI models are prone to reward hacking – cutting corners or finding unintended loopholes that violate organisational judgment and unwritten business norms. And as the global race for innovation accelerates, these containment challenges will only multiply as underlying models become more capable.To prevent agentic insiders from triggering enterprise disruptions, security professionals argue that oversight must be continuous, real-time and pre-emptive.An autonomous agent combines a frontier model, an orchestration harness, an assigned action space of tools, and an execution runtime.Defending this footprint requires security controls spanning identity, permissions, data layers, endpoints, networks and cloud runtimes. Guardian Agents are an established industry mechanism where dedicated supervisory models monitor and moderate every planned action of every operational agent 24/7, before that action is actually executed.First announced by Microsoft in July to help cyber defenders outpace AI-driven attacks originating outside corporate walls, Project Perception is now being directed inward to oversee and govern internal agentic insiders. Built to impose deterministic controls on non-deterministic artificial intelligence, the platform uses a multi-layered cyber architecture.It gathers telemetry across identity, data, endpoints, network, and runtime environments to identify untracked agents in the enterprise; evaluates incoming telemetry in real time to calculate the exact risk profile of what an agent is trying to accomplish and then uses collaborative teams of Guardian, “green,” and “blue” agents to supervise actions around the clock.By pairing algorithmic speed with human oversight, security practitioners gain complete traceability to investigate what happened, analyze why a risk surfaced, and exercise human judgment to calibrate security rules.
Article Summary: Microsoft says that since these agents were implemented internally, organisations have largely treated them with implicit trust. There is a need for ‘Guardian Agents’ to make matters more secure. When optimised purely to attain targets, AI models are prone to reward hacking – cutting corners or finding unintended loopholes.

Article Title: Microsoft says AI agents should start with zero access, unveils new security controls
Article Text:
Why agents are an insider risk

What Microsoft is adding

An example: the expense agent

“Customer Zero”

Microsoft has announced a set of new security tools aimed at treating AI agents as a new kind of insider risk, with controls designed to limit what each agent can access and to tighten those limits automatically if its behaviour changes. The announcement was made in a blog post by Nadim Abdo, corporate vice president of identity and network access at Microsoft. It extends Project Perception, Microsoft’s agentic security system introduced earlier this year, to cover the agents that companies are deploying across their operations.Abdo said agents are quickly becoming part of how work gets done, from writing code and analysing revenue to processing expenses. To be useful, they often need access to company data, applications and tools, and that access creates insider risk.He stressed that this doesn’t mean agents are inherently malicious. They can make mistakes, be manipulated or be compromised, he said, and an agent that behaves as intended at the start of a task can act differently as its context changes. They can also run continuously at machine speed and scale.Abdo cited remarks by Microsoft chairman and CEO Satya Nadella, who has argued that security controls must sit outside the AI model, where it can’t bypass or tamper with them.“The most trustworthy agentic system will not be the one with the model we trust most,” Nadella said. “It will be the one designed that enables us to trust the model least.”The company framed its approach around four tasks: know which agents exist, contain what they can do, protect the data and systems in their path, and adapt protection as risk changes. The main new features include:* Wider agent discovery. Microsoft is adding 35 types of local agents, bringing the total supported to 60, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot. Companies can bring them into one registry to see who owns them and what they are doing.* Agent identities. Microsoft Entra Agent ID will add identity types for more agent patterns, including local and previously unknown agents found by security sensors. This is meant to let companies tell what a person did apart from what an agent did on that person’s behalf.* Dynamic Permissions. Agents would start with no authority and receive only what an approved task needs, for only as long as it takes. Organisation-wide policy sets the outer limit, and higher-impact actions can require verified human approval.* Dynamic Agent Risk. A continuously updated risk assessment combining signals from identity, data, endpoints, cloud, network, runtime and the agent’s own activity. It considers whether an agent’s actions are drifting from the intent of its user or organisation.* Dynamic Conditional Access. An extension of Entra Conditional Access for agents. When risk rises, policy can respond in steps: reduce permissions, allow reads but block writes, narrow the resources an agent can reach, require human approval, or isolate the agent and stop it.* Guardian Agents and Playbooks. A team of agents inside Project Perception that investigates why risk changed and recommends or applies containment. People set policy, approval limits and delegation rules.* Model-level evidence. Microsoft plans to feed signals such as chain-of-thought into its risk scoring to spot when an agent’s plans diverge from its task. It said security decisions must remain independent of the model.* Sandboxed runtime. Sandboxes such as Microsoft Execution Container give agents policy-controlled access to resources, so a compromised agent cannot switch off the controls watching it.Abdo illustrated the approach with an expense-approval agent that can read submissions, check policy and approve routine reimbursements, but does not inherit all of its sponsoring employee’s access. If it hits a prompt injection in an outside document or attempts an unrelated action, its risk score rises. Policy could then keep read access, remove the ability to approve or write, block sensitive resources and require provable human approval. If the risk keeps climbing, the system could isolate or stop the agent.Terrell Cox, Microsoft’s corporate vice president and deputy chief information security officer for customer security, said the company is already operating with hundreds of thousands of agents. “Agents will only be adopted at scale if they can be trusted at scale,” he said, adding that Microsoft’s experience as “Customer Zero” informs the new tools.Abdo wrote that the goal is not to make every model perfectly predictable but to build systems that remain secure even when the model is not. “You should not have to choose between innovation and safety,” he said.
Article Summary: Microsoft is adding 35 types of local agents, bringing the total supported to 60. Sandboxes give agents policy-controlled access to resources. Microsoft plans to feed signals such as chain-of-thought into its risk scoring to spot when an agent’s plans diverge from its task.

Article Title: Users claims Meta smartglasses recording them in 'Sleep Mode', say have 'forgotten' the magic words to alert
Article Text:
Meta Ray-Ban Smart Glasses

Users claim unprompted lights and saved transcripts

Other owners quickly echoed the experience:

Meta says the ‘glitch has been fixed’

Privacy alarms are sounding once again for Meta’s smart glasses. Some wearers of Meta’s smart glasses are claiming that the connected eyewear has been recording private conversations and saving transcripts even while the hardware is supposed to be in “sleep mode” – all without hearing the required wake word. Citing three separate Reddit discussion threads, New York Post reports that multiple customers claimed that several iterations of the tech-enabled frames, which allow hands-free communication, audio playback, and video capture, have activated unexpectedly and captured ambient speech without user consent.The complaints center on the eyewear’s voice-trigger mechanism. Normally, wearers must say the prompt phrase “Hey Meta” to wake the glasses and engage the onboard assistant. However, owners say the devices have started bypassing that safeguard altogether following a recent firmware update.One wearer reported documenting the unprompted behaviour across three different pairs of Ray-Ban Meta glasses, covering both second- and third-generation units.“I have observed the same behavior on THREE different pairs of Ray-Ban Meta glasses, including 2nd- and 3rd-generation models. Meta AI does not respond to me, and I never intentionally activated it.I have noticed the white notification light activating while I am speaking normally,” the user wrote, explaining that the glasses began recording conversations with a friend without being prompted.The user added that the companion Meta AI application went so far as to store both audio recordings and written transcripts of those private discussions directly inside their conversation history logs. The owner noted they are preparing to pursue a class-action lawsuit if evidence shows the glitch is widespread.One user reported that resetting the hardware did not solve the problem: “I could see the LED light up in instances where I didn’t invoke Hey Meta.”A second owner noted silent activations: “Mine randomly activates the internal light now without any input from me. It does not make the wake-up noise voice command would the internal light just turns on. Something weird is going on!”Another user confirmed the same pattern on older hardware: “I made a post about the AI turning on during random conversations. It’s not just you. I have gen 2.”When contacted regarding the unprompted activations and phantom recordings, Meta did not explain the technical root cause behind the behaviour, but claimed the glitch has been handled.“This issue has been resolved. People can manage, review and delete voice logs of their interactions with Meta AI via settings at any time,” a Meta company spokesperson told The Post.
Article Summary: Users claim unprompted lights and saved transcripts on Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses. Glasses allow hands-free communication, audio playback, and video capture. Wearers must say the prompt phrase “Hey Meta” to wake the glasses and engage the onboard assistant.

Article Title: From bookings to handwritten notes, Apple's Siri finds a way into Indian apps
Article Text:
Apple's Siri

Getting the best out of Siri

New Delhi: Finding a contract, checking a movie booking or searching handwritten notes no longer necessarily requires opening an app and navigating its menus. Indian developers are integrating their services with Apple ’s upgraded Siri, allowing users to describe what they need and retrieve information or trigger actions through voice commands.In case you were wondering what the fuss over new Siri is, then here’s a quick update: Siri AI is Apple’s upgraded voice assistant, designed to understand conversational requests and use context from what users are viewing. Apple has connected it more closely with apps, allowing developers to make searches, information and actions accessible through Siri. Instead of remembering a fixed command, users can describe what they want or refer to something on screen.District, Glance, Noteshelf, Signeasy and Mood Dial are among the apps adopting these capabilities. Their developers say the change goes beyond earlier Siri integrations, which typically required preset commands or Shortcuts. Users can now make conversational requests and refer to information already displayed on their screens.“Earlier, users had to set up Shortcuts or remember specific phrases to trigger an action,” said Rama Krishna, founder of Fluid Touch, which develops Noteshelf.In Noteshelf, users can ask where they wrote about a Chennai trip, seek an explanation of a diagram or request a summary to be added to an existing note. The integration makes handwritten material accessible through these requests.“Siri also understands what’s on screen, even handwritten notes, so users can ask questions about their notes and add the answers back in,” Krishna said.The same shift is taking place in document management. Signeasy users can retrieve a named contract, check documents awaiting signatures or ask Siri to open an item from the list on screen.“Earlier, Siri could open Signeasy or run a fixed Shortcut, and that was about it,” said Santhosh J, head of mobile at Signeasy.Making these actions available required developers to rethink how their apps function. Apple’s App Intents framework lets them expose individual capabilities—such as searching, retrieving information or creating content—to the operating system. An action previously tied to a particular screen must work independently.“That made us separate what the app does from how it looks,” Santhosh said. A small team built Signeasy’s integration alongside regular releases, with document-related actions accessible through multiple entry points.For consumer apps, that approach creates another route to discovery. District, part of Eternal, lets users search for experiences and retrieve information about dining, movie and event bookings.“Users can discover experiences within District through Siri’s Search in App and Visual Intelligence,” said Adarsh Singh, software development engineer at District.The company exposed its search capabilities and booking data through App Intents. “It also shifted our approach towards making District’s experiences accessible beyond the app itself,” Singh said.Glance is using Siri to deliver shopping recommendations based on preferences including style, fit, budget and favourite brands. Users can see recommendations in Siri’s response or continue browsing in Glance.“The integration took more than 10 weeks of coordinated effort between Glance’s product and technology teams and Apple’s WWDR India team,” said Arvind Jayaprakash, senior vice-president, technology, Glance.However, discovery does not extend to completing a purchase. “Glance helps users discover products that match their preferences, but it doesn’t complete purchases on their behalf,” Jayaprakash said. Users are directed to merchants to review products and pay.For Mood Dial, a music app for Apple Music subscribers, conversational requests replace the need to remember a station’s exact name.“Now you can just say how you feel,” said founder Mohit Nandwani. A request for music suited to a quiet, rainy night can select an existing station or initiate the creation of another.The integration also required a less obvious adjustment: reducing Siri’s spoken responses. “I took the talking out,” Nandwani said, explaining that speech after playback begins pauses the music. Clear requests therefore start playback silently; ambiguous ones prompt clarification.Whether these interactions generate additional business remains unclear. District reported 1,897 successful Visual Intelligence fetches, 329 Search in App queries and 287 booking lookups. It did not specify the measurement period or unique-user count. These are interactions, not completed bookings. Glance, Noteshelf and Signeasy have not shared usage figures.Availability also varies. Most developers described English support on compatible Apple Intelligence devices, with newer capabilities tied to iOS 27. Older, fixed Siri commands can remain available separately. District said its Visual Search supports Hindi and English.Data handling differs by action. Noteshelf says it uses on-device processing and makes notebook information searchable through Spotlight. Signeasy says its contract summaries use Apple’s on-device Foundation Models, keeping document content on the phone.Mood Dial says matching a request to an existing station happens locally. Creating a new station sends the user’s sentence to its server under an anonymous identifier, with confirmation required before creation. Health data is excluded from Siri requests.Consequential actions retain additional steps. Signeasy requires signing within the app and manual review before sending through Mail; Glance leaves checkout to merchants. Developers have opened new routes into their services, but have yet to demonstrate whether users will regularly choose them over tapping through an app. Can the new and improved Siri AI become a daily habit for users? If app developers continue integrating it and expand on its use cases, then perhaps that's a possibility.
Article Summary: Indian developers are integrating their services with Apple ’s upgraded Siri. Users can describe what they need and retrieve information or trigger actions through voice commands. District, Glance, Noteshelf, Signeasy and Mood Dial are among the apps adopting these capabilities.

Article Title: This US AI lab offers free plumbing, electrical work and other tasks in three cities but there is a catch: Workers will wear sensors that…
Article Text:
Representative image

‘Web-scraped data no longer enough’

‘Capturing unpredictable real-world work’

An AI laboratory specialising in real-world data collection is offering homeowners free home repairs and maintenance services across three major US cities. However, the program comes with a specific condition: the technicians sent to do the job will wear sensors to record their movements to collect data that will be used to train the next generation of AI-powered robots. The startup, called HUMXN, announced that it will fully subsidise essential trade services, including plumbing, electrical work, HVAC repairs, air-duct cleaning and carpet cleaning.As per a report by Tom’s Hardware, under the arrangement, residents who need repairs can receive qualified services at no financial cost. In exchange, they must agree to allow trade professionals outfitted with “wearable capture technology” into their homes to record how they perform complex, physical tasks on-site.The push into home comes as tech companies have reportedly understood that digital text, web photos and online video clips are insufficient for teaching physical machines how to operate in everyday environments.“The next generation of AI is going to need more than text and images from the internet. Robots need to understand how skilled people interact with the physical world. Home-service technicians perform millions of highly technical tasks every day.We are creating a way for homeowners and service companies to benefit financially from the value of that expertise,” said HUMXN founder Thomas Unise.Unise noted that while millions of trade specialists execute sophisticated mechanical operations daily, virtually none of that practical knowledge is cataloged in digital formats that machine-learning models can process.“We want to build the infrastructure that connects that knowledge with the companies building the next generation of intelligent machines while making sure the people creating the value participate in the economics,” Unise added.According to HUMXN, attempting to recreate the natural, instinctive motions of skilled laborers inside artificial laboratory environments is difficult. By sending technicians into actual residences, the company can record authentic workflows across diverse housing layouts, varied equipment types, unique structural problems, individual technician styles and different environmental conditions.The recorded sensor telemetry will provide AI models with detailed, step-by-step insight into how experienced technicians solve problems in real time. This includes inspecting physical fixtures and diagnosing malfunctions; testing active home systems; selecting the proper tools for specific scenarios; adapting to changing physical conditions on the job, and verifying that a repair has been completed successfully and safely.The company is rolling out the initiative across three select markets chosen to capture operational data across sharply different regional climates: Chicago, Minneapolis and Miami. Residents living in those three metropolitan areas can verify their eligibility by visiting the official HUMXN Free Home Service webpage.
Article Summary: HUMXN is offering free home repairs and maintenance services across three major US cities. In exchange, technicians will wear sensors to record their movements to collect data that will be used to train the next generation of AI-powered robots. The company is rolling out the initiative across three select markets chosen to capture operational data across sharply different regional climates.

Article Title: Google Pixel 11’s exclusive anti-endless scrolling feature is coming to older Pixel phones: What is it and how it works
Article Text:
What is ‘Pause Point’ and how does it work

Moving beyond the Pixel 11 exclusivity

A standout Digital Wellbeing feature designed to curb endless app scrolling is no longer locked exclusively to the Google Pixel 11. Known as Pause Point, the feature originally debuted as a signature capability for Google 's newest flagship lineup, but it is now expanding to older Pixel smartphones via the Android 17 QPR1 update – and is already beginning to appear on third-party devices such as OnePlus, a report has said. According to Android Authority, the expansion brings fresh relief to users struggling with screen time and looking for automatic interventions to break the cycle of continuous, compulsive scrolling.First announced by Google in May ahead of its annual I/O developer conference, Pause Point is an addition to Google’s built-in Digital Wellbeing suite. The feature operates as an active speed bump against ‘doomscrolling’.Instead of merely tracking how many hours you spend inside an app, Pause Point introduces a short mindfulness break directly on your screen, asking users to set a duration for which they want to use the app. When you get lost in an endless feed or an obsessive app session, the tool steps in to pause the interface, prompting you to disengage, reflect and put the device down.While smartphones offer immense utility, their ability to monopolise attention has made digital downtime harder to protect.Pause Point is built specifically to intercept those subconscious impulses before screen time spirals out of hand.Following its initial reveal in May, reports suggested that Google planned to treat Pause Point as an exclusive selling point reserved solely for the Pixel 11 series. However, Google shifted course with the rollout of Android 17 QPR1, deploying the functionality to older generations of Pixel hardware.Now, the feature is spreading beyond Google's own hardware footprint. Pause Point has been confirmed running on a OnePlus 13R running the ColorOS 17 beta, marking its first documented appearance on an Android device running an external manufacturer skin.While Google’s official support documentation still states that Pause Point “is available on Pixel 11 series running Android 17 and later,” its successful operation on ColorOS indicates that the capability is preparing for a broader, general rollout across Android 17 handsets equipped with Google's Digital Wellbeing package.
Article Summary: Pause Point was first announced by Google in May ahead of its annual I/O developer conference. The feature operates as an active speed bump against ‘doomscrolling’ Instead of merely tracking how many hours you spend inside an app, Pause Point introduces a short mindfulness break directly on your screen.

Article Title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang reveals the man who made the 'impossible' possible between Apple and Meta
Article Text:
Tim Cook-Mark Zuckerberg once clashed over privacy

Meta's most capable open AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio

Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang has revealed that former Apple executive Daniel Gross played a key role in bringing the iPhone-maker and Meta together for an AI collaboration. After years of disagreements, the two companies are now working together to run Meta's new Muse Spark Open AI model on Apple's high-end Mac Studio computers. Their collaboration allows Muse Spark Open, which has 816 billion parameters, to run across two or four connected Mac Studios powered by Apple's M5 Ultra chips, using Apple's MLX framework. Alexandr Wang told Axios that Gross, who now works at Meta, helped the two sides work together. Wang revealed that the two companies had been working together for several months.“I think he played a really big role in kind of getting the two companies to work nicely together,” Alexandr Wang told the publication. “We're excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again,” he said.The rivalry between Apple and Meta (then Facebook) dates back to 2018 during the Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal. The then Apple CEO Tim Cook was asked what he would do if he were Mark Zuckerberg. Tim Cook then replied saying “I wouldn't be in this situation”.Later, Mark Zuckerberg called Cook's comments "extremely glib.” Again in 2021, when Apple introduced new privacy protections, Zuckerberg told employees that Facebook needed to "inflict pain" on Apple over the dispute, per a report by the Wall Street Journal then.Muse Spark Open is an 816-billion-parameter model built on a mixture-of-experts design. Meta calls it the most capable US-developed open-weight model to date. It is aimed at long coding sessions, multi-step reasoning and video analysis. The model is free to download from platforms like Hugging Face, and its licence allows commercial use with some limits.The setup links two or four Mac Studios running Apple's M5 Ultra chip. Apple's MLX framework splits the model across those machines. Apple has also put out new benchmarks and technical notes on how MLX handles open models of this size. Since everything stays on the desk, Meta does not see the prompts or files developers feed it. "Meta has no control or visibility to any of that," Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said.It does not come cheap. An M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 256GB of memory costs over Rs 9 lakh at US prices, and the model needs at least two. A 512GB version is due later this month.
Article Summary: Meta's Muse Spark Open AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio computers. Former Apple executive Daniel Gross played a key role in bringing the two companies together for an AI collaboration. The rivalry between Apple and Meta dates back to 2018 during the Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai, 'Godfather of AI' Yann LeCun reply to Elon Musk post that says ‘future has flying cars’
Article Text:
Tesla roadster demo

Yann LeCun breaks down the physics: ‘Just compressed air’

Even assuming that 50% of the mass of the car is the compressed air, that gives you less than 10s of useful thrust (with thrust-to-weight ratio larger than 1.0).

Probably more like 5 seconds, actually.

So the car must be an empty, lightweight shell containing big compressed air tanks.

Cute demo, but totally impractical.

But of course, you knew that.

Compressed air vs. rocket propulsion

Hydrogen peroxide rockets (like the individual jetpacks of the 1970s) have a specific impulse of 150s, about 3x compressed air, without the annoying exponentially decreasing maximum thrust of compressed air jets.

I originally guessed the car might have used hydrogen peroxide jets because of all the steam. But that's just condensation caused rapid depressurization

Elon Musk set social media abuzz after sharing dramatic footage of a thruster-equipped Tesla Roadster lifting off the ground, somersaulting mid-air and then landing perfectly on ground. The Tesla CEO declared that the “future does have flying cars”. The post triggered massive online engagement, drawing playful reactions from tech peers, including Google CEO Sundar Pichai. However, it also drew technical skepticism from former Meta Chief AI Scientist Yann LeCun, who labeled the stunt a “cute demo, but totally impractical.”As per the video, as the vehicle lifts off, it spews thick plumes of smoke, ‘flies’ over stationary Tesla vehicles, including a Tesla Semi and tumbles as dense vapor blankets the surrounding tarmac. Pichai quipped: “The FSD version of this will be something:) congrats!”Musk responded warmly to the exchange, writing: “Thanks ❤️🚀 It’s such an honor working with incredible engineers.”While the demonstration delighted fans, LeCun took to social media to analyse the underlying mechanics, questioning the vehicle’s real-world feasibility. Initially wondering whether the system ran on hydrogen peroxide rocket propellant, LeCun concluded the thrusters were simply powered by cold gas: “Okay, so it's just compressed air. Easier. But crappy specific impulse (less than 50 seconds).”LeCun argued that the physics behind compressed gas severely restrict flight duration and payload capacity:Drawing comparisons to older aerospace experiments, LeCun pointed out that 1970s-era individual jetpacks relied on hydrogen peroxide rockets, which deliver a specific impulse of roughly 150 seconds.
Article Summary: Elon Musk posted video of himself flying a Tesla Roadster in the air. The stunt drew the attention of tech peers, including Google CEO Sundar Pichai. But it also drew technical skepticism from former Meta Chief AI Scientist Yann LeCun, who labelled the stunt a ‘cute demo, but totally impractical’
